examples.en: That boss is a well-known miser.

examples.ko: 돈을 안 쓴다고 나를 수전노라고 불러요.
examples.en: They call me a miser because I don't spend money.

examples.ko: 수전노처럼 굴지 말고 밥 한 번 사세요.
examples.en: Don't act like a miser; buy us a meal for once.
The miser in the story ended up lonely.

examples.ko: 그 수전노 영감이 동전 하나도 안 내놓았어요.
examples.en: That miserly old man didn't hand over even a single coin.
Even a miser would spend money on family, right?

explain: '구두쇠', '짠돌이'와 비슷하지만 돈에만 집착한다고 비난하는 느낌이 있어서 사람 앞에서 쓰면 실례가 될 수 있어요. 가볍게 놀릴 때는 '짠돌이'나 '구두쇠'를 더 많이 써요. 이야기나 속담 속 인물에도 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 돈을 하나도 안 써서 수전노 같아요.
phrases.en: He never spends any money, so he seems like a miser.
phrases.nuance_ko: '같다'를 붙여 비유로 말할 때 써요. 비난하는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 같다 to make a comparison; it carries a critical tone.

phrases.example: 우리 아버지는 구두쇠라서 잘 안 사 주세요.
phrases.en: My father is stingy, so he rarely buys things for us.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 뜻이지만 '수전노'보다 덜 심하고 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning, but milder than 수전노 and more common in daily talk.

phrases.en: My friend is a penny-pincher, but he has a warm heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가볍게 놀리듯이 돈을 아끼는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used playfully for someone who saves every penny.

explain_en: It is close to '구두쇠' and '짠돌이', but it carries a tone of blaming someone for caring only about money, so saying it to a person can be rude. For light teasing, '짠돌이' or '구두쇠' are used more. It also often appears for characters in stories and sayings.

examples.en: My uncle runs a small shop in the countryside.
I called my uncle yesterday to check in.

examples.ko: 아버지의 동생인 숙부가 우리 집에 오셨어요.
examples.en: My father's younger brother, my uncle, came to our house.
The family gathered at my uncle's house for the holiday.

examples.ko: 저는 숙부를 닮았다는 말을 자주 들어요.
examples.en: I often hear that I look like my uncle.

examples.ko: 제가 어릴 때 숙부가 용돈을 자주 주셨어요.
examples.en: When I was little, my uncle often gave me pocket money.

explain: 말할 때는 보통 '삼촌'이라고 하고, '숙부'는 글이나 격식 있는 자리에서 더 많이 써요. 아버지의 남동생만 가리키고, 아버지의 형은 '큰아버지'라고 해요. 어머니 쪽 남자 형제는 '외삼촌'이에요.

phrases.en: My uncle works at a company in Seoul.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 가장 흔히 쓰는 말이에요. '숙부'는 더 격식 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The everyday word. 숙부 is more formal.

phrases.en: My uncle moved last week.
phrases.nuance_ko: '숙부'에 '님'을 붙인 높임 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A respectful form made by adding 님 to 숙부.

phrases.example: 명절에는 숙부 댁에 가서 인사를 드려요.
phrases.en: On holidays I go to my uncle's house to pay respects.
phrases.nuance_ko: '집'의 높임말인 '댁'을 붙여 숙부의 집을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the honorific 댁 to mean the uncle's home.

explain_en: In everyday speech Koreans say 삼촌, while 숙부 appears more in writing and formal settings. 숙부 means only the father's younger brother; the father's older brother is 큰아버지. The mother's brother is 외삼촌.

en: to be naïve; to be simple and honest

examples.en: People in the countryside are generally simple and honest.

examples.ko: 순박한 웃음을 가진 할아버지가 떡을 건네주셨어요.
examples.en: An old man with a simple, honest smile handed me rice cake.

examples.ko: 그는 너무 순박해서 거짓말을 할 줄 몰라요.
examples.en: He is so unaffected that he doesn't know how to lie.

examples.ko: 순박한 마음으로 사람을 대하면 좋은 일이 생겨요.
examples.en: If you treat people with an honest heart, good things happen.
The shop lady's plain, honest way of speaking felt warm and friendly.

examples.ko: 순박해 보이는 청년이 길을 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: A guileless-looking young man showed me the way.

explain: 꾸밈없고 착하며 인정이 있는 사람이나 분위기에 써요. '순진하다'는 세상 물정을 잘 모른다는 느낌이 강하고, '순박하다'는 소박하고 정직하다는 느낌이 더 커요.

phrases.en: He is a truly simple and honest person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꾸밈없고 착한 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an unpretentious, kind person.

phrases.en: That young man looks simple and honest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이나 인상을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an outward impression.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is still naive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세상 물정을 잘 모른다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has a stronger sense of not knowing the ways of the world.

explain_en: It describes a person or atmosphere that is unpretentious, kind and warm-hearted. '순진하다' leans toward not knowing the ways of the world, while '순박하다' emphasizes being plain and honest.

examples.en: My mother is looking for a good husband candidate.
He is popular as a marriage candidate.

examples.ko: 신랑감 소개 좀 해 달라고 부탁했어요.
examples.en: I asked someone to introduce me to a potential husband.
What kind of person would you like your future husband to be?
In the old days, parents picked the groom for you.
Aren't the requirements for a husband too picky?

explain: 결혼식장에 선 '신랑'과 달라서, 앞으로 결혼 상대가 될 만한 남자를 말해요. 여자 쪽은 '신붓감'이라고 해요. '신랑감으로 좋다'처럼 상대를 평가하는 말이라 조심해서 쓰세요.

phrases.en: A sincere person makes a good potential husband.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결혼 상대로 괜찮다는 평가를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when judging someone as a good marriage prospect.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 직업도 좋고 신랑감으로 좋아요.
phrases.en: He has a good job and is good husband material.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 평가하는 말이라 조심해서 써야 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This evaluates a person, so use it carefully.

phrases.en: My aunt is looking for a husband for my cousin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결혼할 만한 상대를 구한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means seeking someone suitable to marry.
phrases.en_equiv: to look for a prospective husband

explain_en: Unlike '신랑' (the groom at the wedding), this means a man who could become a marriage partner. The counterpart for women is '신붓감'. It evaluates a person, as in '신랑감으로 좋다', so use it with care.

en: real authority; real power; influential figure; powerhouse

examples.ko: 그 사람이 회사의 진짜 실세라고 해요.
examples.en: They say that person is the real power in the company.
The secretary known as the one holding real power attended the meeting.

examples.ko: 직함은 낮아도 사실상 실세인 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: Even with a low title, some people are the real power in practice.

examples.ko: 새 대표가 와도 실세는 바뀌지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even after the new CEO arrived, the person with real power didn't change.

examples.ko: 실세 눈치를 보느라 아무도 반대하지 못했어요.
examples.en: Everyone was watching the powerful figure's mood, so nobody could object.
Things go faster when you know who really holds the power.

explain: '대표', '회장' 같은 공식 직위와 달리, 직함이 낮아도 결정에 영향을 주는 사람이면 실세예요. 뉴스에서는 '정권 실세'처럼 쓰고, 회사나 모임에서는 '진짜 실세는 따로 있다'고 말해요.

phrases.en: He is a figure called a power player in the administration.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 정치 이야기를 할 때 많이 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in political news.

phrases.example: 사장보다 비서가 숨은 실세라는 말이 있어요.
phrases.en: People say the secretary, not the president, is the hidden power.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직함은 낮지만 뒤에서 영향을 주는 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to someone with a low title who influences things from behind the scenes.

phrases.en: That person is regarded as the real power in the group.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 그를 실세로 여긴다는 뜻으로, 회사나 모임에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means people regard the person as the one with real influence; used for companies and groups.
phrases.en_equiv: to be regarded as the real power

explain_en: Unlike official posts such as CEO or chairman, someone with a low title is still a '실세' if they sway decisions. In news it is used as '정권 실세', and in companies or groups people say '진짜 실세는 따로 있다' (the real power is someone else).

examples.en: He was always an outsider at school.
I'm an outsider, so gatherings feel a bit uncomfortable.
The movie's hero lives as an outsider.
It is a book that looks at society through an outsider's eyes.
I try not to become an outsider at work.
Outsider artists created a new trend.

explain: 무리나 집단 안에 잘 섞이지 못하거나 밖에 있는 사람을 말해요. 같은 뜻으로 '외톨이'나 '왕따'를 쓰기도 하지만 '왕따'는 괴롭힘의 의미가 강해요. '아웃사이더'는 스스로 선택한 경우에도 써서 반드시 나쁜 말은 아니에요.

phrases.example: 새 학교에서 아웃사이더가 될까 봐 걱정이에요.
phrases.en: I'm worried I'll become an outsider at my new school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무리에 섞이지 못하는 상황이 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone ends up not fitting into a group.

phrases.example: 그는 늘 아웃사이더처럼 혼자 앉아 있어요.
phrases.en: He always sits alone like an outsider.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모임에서 떨어져 있는 모습을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A comparison for someone staying apart from the group.

phrases.en: I was a loner at school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 뜻이지만 '외톨이'는 혼자 있는 쓸쓸한 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning, but '외톨이' feels more lonely.

explain_en: A person who does not mix with a group or stays outside it. 외톨이 and 왕따 are used for similar meaning, but 왕따 strongly implies bullying. 아웃사이더 can be a person's own choice, so it is not always negative.

en: to be wicked; to be atrocious

examples.en: That boss was cruel to his employees.

examples.ko: 동화 속 악독한 마녀가 마을 사람들을 괴롭혀요.
examples.en: The wicked witch in the fairy tale torments the villagers.

examples.ko: 그는 악독한 방법으로 돈을 모은 사람이에요.
examples.en: He is a person who made money by vicious means.
There was no need to speak so cruelly.
I played a wicked character in the movie.
I worked under an owner known for being ruthless.

explain: 마음씨나 하는 짓이 아주 모질고 나쁜 사람이나 행동에 써요. '못됐다'보다 훨씬 강하고, 이야기나 글에서 더 잘 어울려요. '악독하게 굴다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: A wicked person appears in that movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: '악독하다'를 '악독한'으로 활용해서 사람을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form used to describe a person.

phrases.en: The owner treated the workers cruelly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남에게 모질게 대하는 행동을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for treating others harshly.

phrases.en: The stepmother in the story is truly wicked.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 문장을 끝내서 사람의 성격이나 행동을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite sentence-ending form for describing someone's character.

explain_en: It describes a person or action that is extremely cruel and bad at heart. It is far stronger than '못됐다' and fits stories and writing well. A common pattern is '악독하게 굴다'.

examples.en: My son talks like a little old man.
He's ten but acts as mature as an old soul.
My friends call me an old soul.
Don't talk like an old man.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 애늙은이여서 또래와 잘 안 놀아요.
examples.en: That child is an old soul and doesn't play much with kids his age.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 애늙은이 소리를 많이 들었어요.
examples.en: I've heard 'old soul' a lot since I was little.

explain: 나이는 어린데 말과 행동이 어른, 특히 노인처럼 느껴지는 아이를 말해요. 칭찬일 수도 있지만 아이답지 않다는 아쉬움이 담길 수도 있어서 말투에 따라 느낌이 달라요.

phrases.example: 저는 어릴 때부터 애늙은이 소리를 들었어요.
phrases.en: I was called an old soul ever since I was little.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주변에서 그렇게 불렀다는 뜻이고, 칭찬일 수도 아닐 수도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means others called you that; it may or may not be praise.
phrases.en_equiv: to be called an old soul

phrases.en: A child who seems like a little old person lives next door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나이에 비해 너무 어른스러운 아이를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a child who is too mature for their age.
phrases.en_equiv: a child like a little old man

phrases.en: That child is really mature.
phrases.nuance_ko: '애늙은이'보다 부드러운 칭찬으로 쓰기 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A gentler compliment than 'aeneureuni'.

explain_en: It refers to a young person whose words and behavior feel adult, especially old-fashioned. It can be praise, but it can also carry a note of regret that the child isn't childlike, so the feel depends on the tone.

en: child who acts like an adult

examples.ko: 우리 아들은 애어른처럼 말해서 웃음이 나요.
examples.en: My son talks like a little adult, which makes me laugh.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 애어른이라는 말을 자주 들었어요.
examples.en: Since I was little, I was often called an old soul.
My younger sibling acts like a little adult for his age.
She matured early and became like a little adult.
I'm proud of the child who acts so mature.

examples.ko: 부모님을 도우려고 애어른이 된 딸이 안쓰러워요.
examples.en: I feel sorry for my daughter, who grew up too fast to help her parents.

explain: 나이는 어리지만 말이나 행동이 어른 같은 아이를 말해요. '어른스럽다'와 비슷하지만 '애어른'은 아이가 너무 일찍 어른이 된 것 같아 안쓰러운 느낌이 들 때도 있어요. 칭찬일 수도, 걱정하는 말일 수도 있어서 상황을 보고 판단해야 해요.

phrases.en: My daughter acts like a little adult.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이가 어른 같다고 말할 때 가장 쉽게 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easiest way to say a child seems like an adult.
phrases.en_equiv: to be like a little adult

phrases.en: My younger sibling acts like a little adult.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말이 아니라 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about behavior rather than speech.
phrases.en_equiv: to act like a little adult

phrases.en: My friends call me a little adult.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람이 그렇게 부를 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when others call someone this.
phrases.en_equiv: to call someone a little adult

explain_en: It describes a child who speaks or acts like an adult. It is similar to '어른스럽다', but '애어른' can also carry a feeling of pity, as if the child grew up too early. It can be praise or concern, so judge from the situation.

examples.en: If parents spoil a child too much, the child becomes ill-mannered.
Grandmother raises her grandchild by indulging him.
I decided not to raise my child by spoiling him.
He grew up in an indulgent atmosphere, so he has no patience.
Please don't keep indulging him just because he's the youngest.
I regret having spoiled him so much.

explain: 아이가 원하는 것을 다 들어주고 받아 주는 것을 말하고, 버릇없게 만든다는 부정적인 느낌이 들어 있어요. '아이를 오냐오냐하다'나 '오냐오냐 키우다'처럼 주로 아이에게 써요.

phrases.en: Grandma raises her grandchild by indulging every wish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이의 요구를 다 받아 주며 키우는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes raising a child by granting every demand.

phrases.example: 부모가 달라는 걸 다 오냐오냐해 줘요.
phrases.en: The parents give in to everything the child asks for.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원하는 것을 거절하지 않고 계속 들어줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone never refuses and keeps granting requests.

phrases.example: 아이의 응석을 다 받아 주면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You shouldn't give in to all of a child's spoiled behavior.
phrases.nuance_ko: '오냐오냐하다'와 비슷하지만 어리광을 받아 준다는 점이 더 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '오냐오냐하다' but more clearly about indulging childish whining.

explain_en: It means giving in to everything a child wants, and it carries a negative sense of making the child ill-mannered. It is mostly used for children, as in '아이를 오냐오냐하다' or '오냐오냐 키우다'.

en: to be stubborn; to be obstinate

examples.ko: 할아버지는 한번 정하면 안 바꾸실 만큼 완고하세요.
examples.en: My grandfather is so stubborn that he never changes what he decides.

examples.ko: 아버지의 완고한 태도 때문에 대화가 잘 안 돼요.
examples.en: Because of my father's stubborn attitude, we can't talk well.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 자기 생각이 옳다고 완고하게 주장했어요.
examples.en: He stubbornly insisted that his own idea was right.

examples.ko: 나이가 들수록 사람이 완고해지는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think people get more set in their ways as they age.

examples.ko: 완고하기로 소문난 부장님이 이번엔 의견을 받아들였어요.
examples.en: The manager, known for being stubborn, accepted the opinion this time.
He is so stubborn that he is really hard to persuade.

explain: 자기 생각이나 방식을 잘 바꾸지 않는 성격에 써요. '고집이 세다'와 비슷한데, '완고하다'는 더 딱딱하고 나이 든 분의 오래된 생각이나 보수적인 태도에 자주 어울려요. 칭찬으로는 잘 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: He is a stubborn person, so he's hard to persuade.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각을 잘 바꾸지 않는 사람을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a person who rarely changes his mind.

phrases.example: 아버지는 너무 완고해서 제 말을 안 들으세요.
phrases.en: My father is so stubborn that he doesn't listen to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어요' 형태로 누군가의 고집스러운 성격을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite -아/어요 form, used to describe someone's obstinate nature.

phrases.example: 동생은 고집이 세서 말을 잘 안 들어요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling is stubborn and doesn't listen well.
phrases.nuance_ko: '완고하다'보다 일상적이고 모든 나이에 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: More everyday than 완고하다 and usable for any age.

explain_en: It describes a person who does not easily change their opinions or ways. It is similar to '고집이 세다', but '완고하다' is stiffer and often fits an older person's old-fashioned or conservative attitude. It is rarely used as a compliment.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 요조숙녀 같다는 말을 자주 들었어요.
examples.en: Since I was little, I've often been told I'm like a refined young lady.

examples.ko: 언니는 평소에 요조숙녀인 척하지만 사실 장난꾸러기예요.
examples.en: My older sister acts like a demure lady usually, but she's actually a prankster.
Today I sat quietly like a proper lady.
Being told to act like a proper lady feels like a burden.
There was a time when my dream was to be a refined lady.
I changed the way I speak because I wanted to look like a refined lady.

explain: 얌전하고 품위 있는 여성을 가리키는 다소 예스러운 말이에요. 요즘에는 칭찬보다 '요조숙녀인 척하다', '요조숙녀 같다'처럼 농담이나 놀림으로 더 많이 써요. 사람에게 직접 쓰면 구식이거나 성별을 따지는 말로 들릴 수 있어요.

phrases.en: She behaves like a graceful lady in front of her friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얌전한 척하는 모습을 놀리듯 말할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to tease someone for acting demure.
phrases.en_equiv: to act like a graceful lady

phrases.example: 동생이 요조숙녀 흉내를 내서 다들 웃었어요.
phrases.en: My younger sister imitated a graceful lady and everyone laughed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일부러 우아한 척하는 장난스러운 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for playful, deliberate pretending to be elegant.

phrases.example: 그 배우는 젊을 때 요조숙녀라고 불렸어요.
phrases.en: That actress was called a graceful lady when she was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예전에 얌전하고 품위 있다는 평을 들었다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone used to be known as demure and refined.
phrases.en_equiv: to be called a graceful lady

explain_en: It is a somewhat old-fashioned word for a demure, dignified woman. Today it is used more as a joke or tease, as in '요조숙녀인 척하다' or '요조숙녀 같다', than as real praise. Said directly to someone, it can sound dated or gender-stereotyped.

examples.ko: 제 딸은 작은 일에도 우는 울보예요.
examples.en: My daughter is a crybaby who cries over small things.

examples.ko: 영화만 보면 눈물이 나서 저는 울보가 돼요.
examples.en: I turn into a crybaby whenever I watch a movie.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 형은 울보라고 놀림을 받았어요.
examples.en: When he was little, my older brother got teased for being a crybaby.

examples.ko: 친구가 울보인 줄 몰랐는데 오늘 많이 울었어요.
examples.en: I didn't know my friend was such a crybaby, but my friend cried a lot today.

examples.ko: 우리 아기는 낮에는 울보가 아니라서 편해요.
examples.en: Our baby isn't a crybaby during the day, so it's easy.

examples.ko: 졸업식에서 울보 선생님이 제일 먼저 눈물을 보였어요.
examples.en: At the graduation, our teacher, who cries easily, was the first to tear up.

explain: '울보'는 잘 우는 사람을 조금 놀리거나 귀엽게 부르는 말이에요. 아이한테 많이 쓰지만 친한 어른끼리 장난으로도 써요. 진지한 자리에서 어른에게 쓰면 무례할 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The baby who cries a lot finally fell asleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘 우는 아기를 귀엽게 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A cute way to call a baby who cries a lot.

phrases.example: 엄마가 아기에게 '울보야, 그만 울어.' 하고 말해요.
phrases.en: The mother says to the baby, "Crybaby, stop crying."
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 직접 부를 때 쓰는 반말 말투예요. 친한 사이나 아이에게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to call someone directly, used with kids or close friends.

phrases.en: I cried like a crybaby after the movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: '처럼'을 붙여 많이 운 모습을 비교해서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '처럼' to compare how much someone cried.

explain_en: 울보 is a slightly teasing or affectionate word for someone who cries easily. It is mostly used for children, but close adults also use it jokingly. Using it seriously on an adult can sound rude.

examples.en: At the museum I saw how primitive people lived.
Primitive people made tools out of stone and used them.

examples.ko: 아이가 원시인 옷을 입고 파티에 갔어요.
examples.en: The child went to the party in a caveman costume.
I read a story about primitive people discovering fire.

examples.ko: 스마트폰 없이 사니까 원시인이 된 기분이에요.
examples.en: Living without a smartphone makes me feel like a caveman.
They say primitive people lived in caves.

explain: '원시인'은 아주 오래전에 살던 사람을 말해요. 요즘 사람에게 쓰면 기술이나 문화에 어둡다고 놀리는 말이 될 수 있어서 조심해요. 가볍게는 '나는 원시인이야'처럼 장난으로 써요.

phrases.example: 캠핑장에서 하루 동안 원시인처럼 살아 봤어요.
phrases.en: I lived like a caveman for a day at the campsite.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-처럼'을 붙여 불편하고 단순하게 사는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -처럼 it describes living in a simple, inconvenient way.

phrases.en: Without my phone, I feel like a caveman.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기술이 없어서 불편하다고 장난으로 말할 때 써요. 다른 사람에게 쓰면 놀리는 말이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: A joking way to say you feel behind without technology. Said about others, it becomes teasing.

phrases.en: People in primitive times used fire.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원시인이 살던 아주 오래된 시대를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the very ancient age when primitive people lived.

explain_en: '원시인' means people who lived in very ancient times. Used on a modern person it can mock them as out of touch with technology, so be careful. People jokingly say it about themselves, as in '나는 원시인이야'.

examples.ko: 말과 행동이 다른 그 사람은 위선자예요.
examples.en: That person whose words and actions differ is a hypocrite.
I don't want to become a hypocrite.
More people have started calling him a hypocrite.

examples.ko: 겉으로만 착한 척하는 위선자는 오래 못 가요.
examples.en: A hypocrite who only pretends to be nice doesn't last long.

examples.ko: 영화 속 위선자의 정체가 드러나는 장면이 인상적이에요.
examples.en: The scene where the hypocrite in the movie is exposed is impressive.

examples.ko: 제 자신이 위선자처럼 느껴져서 마음이 불편했어요.
examples.en: I felt like a hypocrite myself, and it made me uncomfortable.

explain: 겉으로만 착한 척하는 사람을 가리키는 꽤 센 말이라서, 사람에게 직접 쓰면 크게 싸울 수 있어요. 말과 행동이 다르다는 점이 핵심이라 자기 자신을 돌아볼 때 '위선자 같아요'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: I'm strict with others, so I feel like a hypocrite.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자신을 돌아보며 부드럽게 쓸 수 있는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer way to use the word when reflecting on yourself.

phrases.example: 말만 하고 행동하지 않으면 위선자로 보여요.
phrases.en: If you only talk and don't act, you look like a hypocrite.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남에게 그렇게 비친다는 뜻이라 직접 비난하는 것보다 덜 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means that's how you appear, which is less harsh than accusing directly.

phrases.example: 함부로 사람을 위선자라고 부르면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You shouldn't carelessly call someone a hypocrite.
phrases.nuance_ko: 센 말이라서 직접 부르면 다툼이 될 수 있다는 점을 알아 두세요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is a strong word, so calling someone this can cause a fight.

explain_en: This is a fairly strong word for someone who only pretends to be good, so saying it to a person's face can start a big fight. The key point is that words and actions differ, which is why people also use it about themselves, as in '위선자 같아요'.

en: to praise oneself; to boast of oneself

examples.en: My friend who praises his own cooking is funny.
Don't boast too much; let's wait for the results.

examples.ko: 그는 발표 내내 자기 성과를 자화자찬했어요.
examples.en: He praised his own results throughout the presentation.
Working with someone who keeps praising himself is tiring.

examples.ko: 스스로 자화자찬하는 건 쑥스러워서 못 해요.
examples.en: I'm too shy to praise myself like that.
It's okay to pat yourself on the back once in a while.

explain: '자랑하다'보다 스스로 자기를 칭찬하는 모습이 두드러지고 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. 하지만 가볍게 장난스러운 말투로 '자화자찬 좀 하자면'처럼 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 자화자찬 좀 하자면, 저는 요리를 꽤 잘해요.
phrases.en: If I may toot my own horn, I'm quite good at cooking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장난스럽고 가볍게 자기 자랑을 시작할 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A light, playful way to start boasting about oneself.

phrases.en: His self-praising way of talking is uncomfortable to hear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 붙여서 자기 자랑이 많은 말투를 비판할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a noun to criticize a boastful way of speaking.

phrases.en: He was busy praising his own results.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 칭찬만 계속하는 모습을 비꼬듯 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used a bit sarcastically for someone who does nothing but praise themselves.

explain_en: Compared with '자랑하다', it stresses praising yourself and sounds negative. Still, people use it playfully, as in '자화자찬 좀 하자면' (if I may toot my own horn).

examples.en: He is a mainstream, traditional jazz player.

examples.ko: 정통파 요리사들은 레시피를 잘 바꾸지 않아요.
examples.en: Traditionalist chefs rarely change their recipes.
I like new styles more than the traditional school.

examples.ko: 이 학교는 정통파로 불릴 만큼 방식이 엄격해요.
examples.en: This school is strict enough in its methods to be called orthodox.
The orthodox and reformist sides were at odds for a long time.
We should accept methods that are not the orthodox way too.

explain: 원래의 방식이나 가르침을 그대로 이어 가는 쪽을 말해요. 반대편은 '개혁파'나 '신세대'처럼 새로운 방식을 따르는 쪽이에요. 정치, 학문뿐 아니라 음악이나 요리, 운동 스타일 이야기에도 써요.

phrases.example: 이 식당은 정통파 스타일의 이탈리아 요리를 해요.
phrases.en: This restaurant cooks Italian food in a traditional style.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 방식 그대로라는 점을 강조해서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to stress that it keeps the original way.

phrases.en: That singer is called an orthodox, traditional artist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 집단을 이름 붙여 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when labeling a person or group.

phrases.en: The orthodox group and the reform group disagreed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대되는 쪽과 함께 비교할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when comparing with the opposite side.

explain_en: It refers to the side that carries on the original method or teaching as it was. The opposite side is '개혁파' or newer groups that follow new ways. It is used not only in politics and academics but also for styles of music, cooking and sports.

en: birth; origin (place or background one is born into)

examples.en: That singer was born in Busan.

examples.ko: 서울 태생인 친구가 사투리를 못 알아들어요.
examples.en: My friend, a Seoul native, can't understand the dialect.

examples.ko: 그는 가난한 집안 태생이지만 열심히 일했어요.
examples.en: Though born into a poor family, they worked hard.
I was born abroad, so my Korean is clumsy.
Though our backgrounds differ, we are good friends.
He was born in the countryside, so he likes nature.

explain: 태생은 어디에서, 어떤 집안에서 태어났는지를 말해요. '서울 태생'처럼 '지역 + 태생'으로 가장 많이 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '출신'이 있는데, 출신은 태어난 곳뿐 아니라 졸업한 학교나 직장에도 써요.

phrases.en: My grandmother was born in the countryside.
phrases.nuance_ko: '지역 + 태생' 모양으로 어디에서 태어났는지 말할 때 써요. 도시 이름 대신 '시골'도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Follows the 'place + 태생' pattern to say where someone was born; you can use '시골' instead of a city name.

phrases.en: That actor was born in America.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라 이름에도 붙여서 쓸 수 있어요. 지금 어디에 사는지와는 상관없이 태어난 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also works with country names; it states the birthplace regardless of where the person lives now.

phrases.en: I'm from Daejeon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻으로 쓸 수 있지만 '출신'은 졸업한 학교나 직장에도 써서 '태생'보다 범위가 넓어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can mean the same, but '출신' also covers the school you graduated from or a workplace, so it is broader than '태생'.

explain_en: 태생 tells where or into what family someone was born, most often in the pattern place + 태생, like 서울 태생. 출신 is a close word, but it also covers schools and workplaces one came from, not just birth.

en: to find fault with; to criticize

examples.ko: 그 사람은 남의 일을 항상 흠잡아요.
examples.en: That person always finds fault with other people's work.

examples.ko: 아무리 봐도 흠잡을 데가 없는 발표였어요.
examples.en: No matter how I looked at it, it was a presentation without a flaw.
Don't pick on your friend over small things.

examples.ko: 심사위원들도 그 작품은 흠잡기 어렵다고 했어요.
examples.en: Even the judges said that piece is hard to find fault with.
Nobody criticized my choice.

examples.ko: 남을 흠잡다가 정작 자기 실수는 못 봤어요.
examples.en: He was busy picking on others and missed his own mistake.

explain: 작은 잘못이나 부족한 점을 찾아 말한다는 느낌이라 조금 부정적으로 들려요. '흠잡을 데가 없다'는 완벽하다는 칭찬으로 자주 써요. 일부러 문제를 만들어 괴롭히는 '트집 잡다'와 비슷하지만, '흠잡다'는 정말 있는 흠을 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I don't like people who find fault with others.
phrases.nuance_ko: '흠잡다'를 띄어 쓴 형태로, 같은 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spaced-out version of '흠잡다' with the same meaning.

phrases.en: Don't criticize your friend's mistake; help them.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 마세요'를 붙여 하지 말라고 부탁하거나 권할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-지 마세요' is used to politely ask or advise someone not to do it.

phrases.example: 그 사람의 발표는 흠잡을 데가 없었어요.
phrases.en: His presentation was flawless.
phrases.nuance_ko: 완벽하다는 칭찬으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used as praise meaning perfect.

explain_en: It means pointing out small faults or shortcomings, so it can sound a bit negative. '흠잡을 데가 없다' (there is nothing to criticize) is a common way to praise something as perfect. It is close to '트집 잡다' (to nitpick), but '흠잡다' can also refer to a real flaw.
